_comment: Feeds the Strategy panel on the Design Delivery Board. Source of truth for the narrative: docs/strategy/agent-builder-kpis.md. Edit here, run node scripts/build-tracker-board.mjs, republish the artifact.
bet: We want to be the fastest platform on which someone can configure an AI agent and hear it answer, and then trust it enough to put it in front of customers.

northStar.name: Fast Proven Agents
northStar.definition: Agents created this week that reached a verified first answer inside 15 minutes of active builder time, and then held a real conversation of two or more turns within 14 days.
northStar.currentNote: No test-session event exists in the live console, so this cannot be computed today. Modelled 35–45%. Do not quote it.
northStar.counter: FPA count is reported with no target: at 45% it would need ~33 qualifying new agents a week against a modelled 30–40 company-wide. The rate is the half design owns.
northStar.gaming: Strip the builder to one button that plays a canned demo and time-to-first-answer collapses to 20 seconds while nothing works. FPA falls. That is the test a north star has to pass.

inputs.name: TTFA
inputs.definition: Active time from opening the builder to the agent speaking. Idle gaps over 120s removed, winsorised at 900s, median and p75 only, never the mean.

inputs.name: VTR
inputs.definition: Share of new agents that reach a verified first answer at all within 14 days, however long it took.

inputs.name: SBDR
inputs.definition: Share of agents with a verified first answer that publish and take a first production call within 24h, under 30 minutes of total active time.

inputs.name: SAR
inputs.definition: Share of accounts with a proven agent that create a second one within 28 days. The business is expansion-led, so a first-agent-only metric looks away from the money.

budget.ceilingNote: Past this the session is a failure, not a slow success. It is the smallest natural working block a developer has (Parnin & Rugaber, ICPC 2009), not a sum.

stages.note: First paint to first interaction. The first 10 s decide whether the visit continues (NN/g, 205,873 pages). 3 s of it is our own paint.
Template, import, or one sentence. Parity with Vapi and Retell, not an advantage.
Zero required stack decisions. The 50 s is voice audition: ~3 previews at 8 s plus 26 s to commit.
A working prompt and greeting are already seeded, so the median user edits one line. The writer's path is reported separately.
One click from Hear the opening, two from the header. Machine time here is a Doherty problem, under 400 ms.
12 s human for the mic permission, 8 s join, 5 s warm-up. The only stage that can exceed Nielsen's 10-second limit, so the only one that earns a progress state.
First-turn setup plus playback starting. The runtime clock inside it is time-to-first-audio-byte, a different metric in different units.

guardrails.onBreach: Read the errorStage distribution and re-derive the preflight checks from it

guardrails.name: Evidence-before-live rate
guardrails.onBreach: The speed change loses, even if TTFA won

guardrails.name: Minutes consumed per verified test
guardrails.onBreach: A speed win that multiplies test volume is a direct cost increase at $0.10/min

guardrails.name: External share of FPA
guardrails.onBreach: The week's read does not count. Preview traffic currently falls through to external and must be reclassified first

guardrails.name: Telemetry agreement, client vs server
guardrails.threshold: ≥ 95% · inert until the server emitter exists
guardrails.onBreach: As specified today it compares a client event to another client event and would certify bad data as good

guardrailNote: Three that can stop a ship, one cost counter, two data-quality checks. Not seven: every extra guardrail inflates the sample needed per arm by roughly a third. At ~36 first agents a week most of these are monitors read as trends, not hypothesis tests, and the dashboard says so rather than pretending otherwise.

assumptionNote: Two rules throughout. Kohavi's prior: most changes move key metrics not at all, and at Bing 10–20% do, so every prediction is shown raw and discounted by a third. Plan with the discounted figure. And: powered or directional, never both. Where the sample needed exceeds what this traffic produces, the row states a direction and a review date instead of a number.

next.name: W0 measurement gate
next.why: Ship the test-session operation, fix the three duration bugs, extend the sanitiser allowlist. Nothing in the ledger is readable until this lands.

next.name: Move Deployment after Test, or make it skippable
next.why: The rail asks for a model stack and a deployment channel before the user has heard anything. Largest predicted effect in the pack: +8 to +15 pp first-test rate, −30 to −60 s median TTFA.

next.name: Print measured latency and cost per preset on the slider
next.why: Vapi already does. An unlabelled slider pushes users into manual config to find out what it did.

next.name: Immutable versions with one-click rollback
next.why: The rollback guardrail cannot exist without it, and Retell shipped versioning in May.

next.name: 20-participant moderated first-agent benchmark
next.why: At tens of first agents a week, telemetry will not resolve an 8 pp change for two quarters. This gives every assumption a real baseline in one week.

next.name: Timed competitive cold-start study, published with its method
next.why: Every competitor time claim is an undefined marketing number. Ours should not be.

rules: No property may carry text a user typed. deploy_blocked emits a stable code, never the interpolated reason string, which contains campaign names.
Durations accumulate from visibilitychange deltas, never a tick counter, and are winsorised at 900 s.
trigger 'auto' is excluded from every metric: the demo agent starts a test 150 ms after mount, and left in, the headline speed number would be generated by a setTimeout.
Every new property key must be added to the live console's 48-key sanitiser allowlist or it is dropped silently.
Session replay is off by policy, so struggle is inferred from four separate scalar signals, never summed into one index.

decisions.q: Agora's managed-key list is narrower than this prototype assumes. Do we correct the vendor catalogue?
decisions.why: Agora's pricing page covers ARES and Deepgram for speech to text, OpenAI mini and nano models for language, and MiniMax Turbo and OpenAI TTS-1 for voice. Anthropic and ElevenLabs are not on it, and neither is Azure, which is the default TTS in this build. Corrected against the real list, none of the three presets is actually $0.10/min, and the default agent would need a vendor key, which is the opposite of the pitch. Rebuilding the presets from managed models only is a data change with visible consequences for voices and backups, so it is your call, not mine.

decisions.q: Does a simulation count as a verified first answer, or only a live voice test?
decisions.why: Both clocks are undefined until this is settled, and it changes two assumptions in the ledger.
Without a name, everything server-anchored stays provisional and the north star cannot be computed as defined.

decisions.q: Fast-Proven Rate at 45 percent: accept as the target?
decisions.why: It is 1.15 times the cross-SaaS activation mean, chosen because zero required credentials should beat the mean. Aspirational, not derived. Revisit 8 weeks after the first clean cohort.

decisions.q: Is the 20-participant moderated benchmark funded this quarter?
decisions.why: It is the only instrument that can resolve most of the assumption ledger at this traffic.

decisions.q: Do we publish the competitive cold-start study?
decisions.why: It converts fastest platform from an adjective into an artefact, and it may not flatter us at first.

pricing.headline: Agora charges a flat $0.10 per agent-minute, and the docs say it is the same with your own key. A latency-versus-cost slider changes the Agora bill by nothing.
facts: The rate card is one line: Conversational AI Engine Audio Task, $0.10 per minute, first 300 minutes free. No tier by concurrency, region, modality or model.
Verbatim footnote: the unit price includes the selected speech, language and voice models, and you are charged the same price even if you bring your own key.
Audio minutes bill separately at about $0.00099 per participant minute, so the old "$0.10/min, all in" line was falsifiable on Agora's own worked example. It is gone.

The managed-key list is ARES and Deepgram for speech to text, OpenAI GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5-nano and GPT-5-mini for language, and MiniMax Turbo and OpenAI TTS-1 for voice. Anything else adds a second bill from that vendor directly.

Agora's own latency budget sums to about 1,620 ms at the minimums, and the single biggest lever is the silence-detection setting at 640 ms by default, not the model bundle. The badge says model time and names what it excludes.
pricing.change: The axis is now Fastest, Balanced, Most capable. Two badges: speed, which moves, and price, which is a state until a slot leaves the managed key.
